themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 3 this week compared to a baseline average of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either a single major incident or coordinated illegal tree removal activity emerging in East Harlem.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
No prior context in 90-day complaint history; represents entirely new pattern
reporting_angles: Locate the specific trees or sites affected; interview Parks Department about removal requests and enforcement
Investigate whether complaints cluster geographically (development site, single property owner, or distributed)

themes_detail.label: Construction/Plumbing Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped to 16 last week versus a baseline average of 5.9 per week—a 172% spike (z-score: 4.1)—coinciding with 459 DOB building permits filed in the last 90 days (385 alterations), suggesting construction quality or code compliance problems amid heavy renovation activity.
evidence: 16 construction/plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (172% increase)
459 DOB permits filed in past 90 days, with 385 filed as 'Alteration' work
General plumbing remains a top-10 complaint category (684 complaints over 90 days); spike suggests acute degradation
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for complaint locations and cross-reference with recent DOB permit locations to map hotspots
Interview residents in buildings undergoing major alterations; request DOB inspection records and violation data

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Street Cleanliness Decline
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged 700% to 3 complaints two weeks ago (vs. 0.4 weekly baseline, z-score: 5.42), and street sweeping complaints jumped 1100% to 3 complaints two weeks ago (vs. 0.2 weekly baseline, z-score: 6.35)—paired with a long-standing community board request for 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning'—indicating a public health and neighborhood quality-of-life crisis.
evidence: 3 graffiti complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
3 street sweeping complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Community board has filed repeated requests to 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning' (DSNY), indicating this is a chronic unfunded need
reporting_angles: Obtain Sanitation Department street-sweeping schedules and actual route data for CD 111; identify missed blocks
Document current graffiti conditions with photos; interview residents and business owners about impact on quality of life and property values

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints more than doubled to 14 two weeks ago versus a baseline average of 5.8 per week—a 144% spike (z-score: 4.03)—suggesting emerging traffic or street-racing activity in the district.
evidence: 14 vehicle noise complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (144% increase, z-score: 4.03)
Community board has filed repeated requests to 'Hire additional traffic enforcement agents' (NYPD), signaling this is a systemic enforcement gap
Concurrent with street/sidewalk noise spike (339 complaints in 90-day baseline); suggests broader noise enforcement failure
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD about traffic enforcement staffing and response times; cross-reference with precinct complaint data
Speak with residents and business owners in noisy corridors (likely along major avenues like 3rd, 5th, 125th); document timing and patterns

themes_detail.label: Water and Sewer System Stress
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints spiked 586% to 6 two weeks ago (vs. 0.9 weekly baseline, z-score: 6.57), and sewer complaints jumped 554% to 9 three weeks ago (vs. 1.4 weekly baseline, z-score: 4.08)—combined with a long-standing DEP capital budget request—suggesting infrastructure strain during warm weather or a developing system failure.
evidence: 6 water conservation complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.9 weekly average (586% spike, z-score: 6.57)
9 sewer complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 1.4 weekly average (554% spike, z-score: 4.08)
Community board has filed repeated 'Other capital budget requests for DEP' (Department of Environmental Protection), indicating chronic infrastructure underfunding
reporting_angles: Request DEP asset condition reports and planned capital projects for CD 111; compare to complaint clusters
Interview DEP spokesperson about aging water and sewer lines; cross-reference complaint data with main breaks or service advisories
